_about: PRO batch 51: the cross-era pool, set A.

scenarios.title: The Autograph Session
scenarios.text: A mall signing runs three hours over, and the line still wraps around the food court. A man near the back has driven six hours with his son, who is wearing your jersey.

choices.label: Stay until the last one
choices.result: You sign for the last person in line at nine at night, hand cramping. The man with his son cries, and so does the mall manager, and your phone fills up with photos.

choices.label: Speed it up
choices.result: Faster signatures without losing the names or the eye contact. Everyone in line gets one, nobody leaves empty-handed, and you're home by eight with enough left to make dinner.

choices.label: Find the man with his son
choices.result: You find the man and his son in line and bring them to the front. You talk for ten minutes about kicking in the backyard, and the boy keeps the pen.

scenarios.title: The Playoff Push
scenarios.text: The city has noticed the team: flags on cars, players' faces on billboards, and everyone wanting a piece of the players in the last month of the season.

choices.label: Say yes to the city
choices.result: Yes to the hospital visits, the radio, the school assemblies. You're tired by Thursday every week, and the city loves the team, and you find you love the city back.

choices.label: Protect your routine
choices.result: You protect your routine like a fortress, saying no to almost everything politely. The city gets your kicks, not your evenings, and your legs feel fresh in December.

choices.label: Bring the unit with you
choices.result: You do every appearance with the snapper and {holder} beside you. The three specialists become a city favorite, with their own segment on the morning radio show.

scenarios.title: A Season Going Nowhere
scenarios.text: The season's slipping away. The locker room has started counting days until the offseason, and the young players are already comparing vacation plans at their lockers.

choices.label: Keep the standards
choices.result: You keep the standards: the same routine, the same effort, the same early mornings. The young players notice, and two of them start showing up early beside you.

choices.label: Talk to {backup}
choices.result: You take {backup} aside and talk about what a lost season is actually for. It's the most useful conversation either of you has all year, and they start staying late.

choices.label: Look after your body
choices.result: You look after your body in the meantime. A lost season is a chance to heal the small things, and you use every week of it, quietly, with the trainers.

scenarios.title: After the Game
scenarios.text: A teammate's night out after a home game starts at a quiet restaurant and keeps moving: a club, then an after-party, then somewhere you'd rather not be at three in the morning.

choices.label: Leave after dinner
choices.result: Dinner, the best stories of the night, and home by eleven. The teammates call you boring in the group chat, and you're the freshest player in Monday's meeting.

choices.label: Get your teammate home
choices.result: You talk your teammate into a car home at midnight, which takes forty minutes of arguing. He's furious with you that night, then quietly grateful by Tuesday.

choices.label: Stay to the end
choices.result: To the end, and beyond it. A photo from the after-party is everywhere by Monday morning, and {coach} wants to see you before the team meeting starts.

scenarios.title: The Supplement Sponsor
scenarios.text: A supplement company offers you a lucrative deal for a product the league hasn't approved. It isn't banned, exactly, and the rep says nobody will ever check.

choices.label: Ask the league first
choices.result: You ask the league's office first, in writing. The answer comes back no within a week, the rep stops calling, and you never have to wonder what was in it.

choices.label: Find an approved sponsor
choices.result: Your agent finds a sponsor with an approved product within a month. It's less money and far less worry, and the company turns out to be lovely to work with.

choices.label: Sign the deal
choices.result: You sign. The money is good for three months, and then the league's letter arrives, and your name is in the story everyone is reading on Monday morning.

scenarios.title: The Video
scenarios.text: Someone at a crowded bar is filming on their phone while a stranger tries to start a fight with you, poking your chest and saying things about your last kick.

choices.label: Walk away
choices.result: Your jacket, your keys, and out the door, without a word. The video shows a kicker leaving a bar calmly, which is a very boring video, and nobody shares it.

choices.label: Find security
choices.result: You find security, and the stranger is escorted out. You finish your dinner with {best_friend}, shaken and fine, and {best_friend} makes you laugh about it by dessert.

choices.label: Shove him back
choices.result: One shove back, just one. It's on every channel by morning, with a headline about you and not him, and the club's lawyers are calling before breakfast.

scenarios.title: The Friend Who Bets
scenarios.text: An old friend who bets on games calls to catch up, and halfway through asks what you know about the starting quarterback's ankle. He laughs like it's nothing.

choices.label: End the call
choices.result: You end the call politely and immediately. You tell the team's security director the next morning, because that's the rule, and the director thanks you for coming in.

choices.label: Tell him why you can't
choices.result: You explain clearly why you can't: it's the one thing that ends careers. He apologizes, embarrassed, and you don't hear from him again, which hurts more than you expected.

choices.label: Tell him what you know
choices.result: You tell him what you know, casually. A week later the league's investigators have his phone records, and your name is in them, next to the date of the call.

scenarios.title: The Party House
scenarios.text: A teammate rents a big house for the bye week, and the guest list is long: players, friends, people nobody seems to know. The pictures are already online by Friday.

choices.label: Stop by for an hour
choices.result: An hour, a few laughs, and gone before it gets out of hand. You're the only one in Monday's meeting who isn't hiding from the coaches, and that's noticed.

choices.label: Spend the bye with family
choices.result: You spend the bye week at home with family. You see the photos later on your phone and are very glad you aren't in a single one of them.

choices.label: Stay all weekend
choices.result: The whole weekend. On Monday a neighbor's complaint and a stack of photos land on the general manager's desk, and your name is on the list he reads out.

scenarios.title: The New Car
scenarios.text: Your new car does zero to sixty in three seconds, and the highway is empty at midnight. A teammate in the passenger seat grins and says, 'Let's see it.'

choices.label: Drive home at the limit
choices.result: Home at the speed limit, with your teammate groaning the whole way. The car stays perfect, your record stays clean, and he admits at the door it was probably smart.

choices.label: Take it to a track day
choices.result: You book a track day for the bye week, legal and supervised and loud. You and your teammate get the speed out of your system safely, with helmets on.

choices.label: See what it can do
choices.result: You see what it can do on the empty highway. The flashing lights in your mirror arrive at a hundred and twenty, and the story arrives the next morning.

choices.label: Remember how that ended
choices.result: You remember college, the flashing lights and the long night after. You hand your teammate control of the radio instead and drive home slowly, both of you singing badly.
choices.lock_text: having raced on the street in college

scenarios.title: The Rant
scenarios.text: It's two in the morning and you've written four paragraphs about the general manager on your phone. They're articulate, they're furious, and your thumb is over the button.

choices.label: Delete it and sleep
choices.result: Deleted, and then sleep. In the morning you're very glad you did, and you tell {holder} about it as a joke over breakfast, which makes it smaller still.

choices.label: Send it to your agent instead
choices.result: You send it to your agent instead of the world. Your agent calls at seven, agrees with half of it privately, and promises to raise the fair half properly.

choices.label: Post it
choices.result: Posted. By breakfast it's on every sports show, by lunch the general manager has read it twice, and by dinner you have a meeting nobody wants to attend.

choices.label: Remember the last time
choices.result: You remember the last time in full: the apology, the week of headlines. You put the phone in a drawer until morning and delete it with coffee.
choices.lock_text: having learned the hard way online before

scenarios.title: Released for Conduct
scenarios.text: After a last chance and another strike, the club is done with you. The general manager tells you in his office, with a lawyer present and the door closed.

choices.label: Accept it with dignity
choices.result: No argument and no excuses. You shake his hand, clean out your locker, and leave without a scene. It's the worst day of your career, and you know it was earned.

choices.label: Fight it publicly
choices.result: A statement, an appeal, a lawyer of your own. It drags on for a month and changes nothing, except how the next club sees you when your name comes up.

choices.label: Call {parent} from the parking lot
choices.result: You call {parent} from the parking lot. There's a long quiet, then {parent} says they're still proud of who you can be. You write that down later.

scenarios.title: The Setup
scenarios.text: A teammate's spouse has decided you need to meet their friend, and dinner is Saturday at their house whether you like it or not. There's a seating chart.

choices.label: Go with an open mind
choices.result: You go with an open mind. The friend is funny and kind, and you agree to coffee next week, which surprises everyone at the table, including you.

choices.label: Go, but just as friends
choices.result: You go, and say clearly before dessert that it's as friends. Everyone relaxes at once, the seating chart is forgotten, and you have a genuinely good evening.

choices.label: Politely decline
choices.result: A polite decline and a bottle of good olive oil for the host. They take it well, and they try again in the spring with a different friend and a bigger chart.

scenarios.title: The Profile
scenarios.text: Someone screenshots your dating profile, and it ends up on a fan account with a caption you definitely didn't write. Your teammates have printed it out.

choices.label: Laugh about it
choices.result: You sign the printout and pin it to your own locker. The teammates lose interest within a day, {holder} keeps a copy anyway, and the fan account apologizes.

choices.label: Delete the profile
choices.result: You delete the profile and decide on a quieter way of meeting people, through friends. It's a relief, and the evenings feel like yours again almost at once.

choices.label: Ask for it to be taken down
choices.result: You ask the fan account politely to take it down. It does, and posts an apology that's almost funnier than the caption, which you quietly screenshot yourself.
